original_target.title: Does the marked area spectrum determine a symplectic billiard table up to affine equivalence?
original_target.area: Symplectic billiards and geometric inverse problems

full_original_statement:
For a smooth, strictly convex planar domain $`\Omega`$ with everywhere positive boundary curvature, let $`M_\Omega(q)`$ be the maximum area of a simple convex $`q`$-gon inscribed in $`\partial\Omega`$, for each integer $`q\geq 3`$. If two such domains have $`M_{\Omega_1}(q)=M_{\Omega_2}(q)`$ for every $`q\geq3`$, must an affine map carry $`\Omega_1`$ to $`\Omega_2`$?

This sequence is the marked area spectrum of the associated symplectic billiard. Its Mather $`\beta`$-function satisfies $`\beta(1/q)=-2M_\Omega(q)/q`$; knowing the entire $`\beta`$-function supplies at least these values. Affine equivalence here includes reflections; otherwise a reflected asymmetric table would be an immediate obstruction.

sources.scope_comparison: The local target asks global affine equivalence of arbitrary pairs of smooth strictly convex tables sharing every maximal q-gon area, with reflections allowed. The actual final Theorem1.2 requires a C1 isospectral family entirely in an axially symmetric sufficiently near-ellipse class. It proves equi-affinity only within that class and family. This neither gives global pairwise marked-spectrum injectivity nor a counterexample. The primary theorem text was readable in publisher search extraction, although direct HTML open returned a dynamic template. No later matching full announcement was found.
